newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's Khatami urges Iraq to free POWs.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Khatami urges Iraq to free POWs.

text.p: Iran's President Mohammad Khatami urged Iraq on Sunday to release Iranians captured during the countries' 1980-1988 war.
The official news agency IRNA said Khatami's call came during a meeting with former Iranian prisoners of war on the anniversary of their release in 1988.
"The Islamic Republic of Iran will do its utmost through international organisations to pressure Iraq to release Iranian POWs," IRNA quoted Khatami as saying.
It said Khatami also called on Iraq to pay reparations for the war in which tens of thousands were killed from both sides.
"President Khatami expressed hope that Iraq will abide by its international commitments and pay reparations for the losses that its aggression inflicted on Iran," IRNA said.
Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, in a speech marking the end of the Iraq-Iran war on August 8, also urged Khatami to free Iraqi POWs in Iran.
Saddam said Iraq had freed all 39,000 Iranian POWs except for one pilot.
Iran has given conflicting figures about its POWs held in Iraq and Khatami made no mention of numbers. Tehran has said in the past that 5,000 to 10,000 prisoners are held by Iraq.
According to the International Committee of the Red Cross, more than 13,000 Iraqi POWs have not been repatriated. Iraq says the number exceeds 20,000.
